userStories.title: One pinned agent-config list covering every supported agent
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Centralize and extend the pinned agent-configuration policy for every supported agent.

**Motivation** — `BASE_PINNED_PATHS` / `BASE_PINNED_NAMES` (`src/bot/checkout.ts`) miss opencode (`.opencode/`, `opencode.json`), gemini (`.gemini/`), codex (`.codex/`), pi (`.pi/`), aider (`.aider.conf.yml`, which can set `test-cmd` and `lint-cmd`), windsurf (`.windsurfrules`), codex's `AGENTS.override.md` and Claude's `CLAUDE.local.md`.

**Approach** — **One pinned-config list (S12).** `BASE_PINNED_PATHS` and `BASE_PINNED_NAMES` move from `src/bot/checkout.ts` to `src/bot/path-policy.ts`, which is pure, and gain `.opencode`, `opencode.json`, `.gemini`, `.codex`, `.pi`, `.aider.conf.yml`, `.windsurfrules` and the names `AGENTS.override.md` and `CLAUDE.local.md`. A new `isPinnedPath(file)` answers "is this repo-relative path agent configuration": equal to or under a `BASE_PINNED_PATHS` entry, or a basename in `BASE_PINNED_NAMES`. `checkout.ts` imports both lists, so the review's pin covers the new entries unchanged.

**Scope** — In: path-policy constants and predicate, checkout imports, @/bot exports and existing real-repo review-pin coverage. Out: US-002 fix protection/reporting; US-003/004 session pin; US-005 scope wiring. The review's own pin (`pinInstructions`) is unchanged apart from reading the longer lists. `.husky/` is matched at the repo root only, and pinned names match case-sensitively, so a `claude.md` that a case-insensitive filesystem treats as `CLAUDE.md` is neither pinned nor protected.

**Interface** — `isPinnedPath(file: string): boolean` (new export of `src/bot/path-policy.ts` and `@/bot`).

`BASE_PINNED_PATHS`. Target: in `src/bot/path-policy.ts`, `[".nax/rules", ".claude", ".cursor", ".mcp.json", ".github/copilot-instructions.md", ".opencode", "opencode.json", ".gemini", ".codex", ".pi", ".aider.conf.yml", ".windsurfrules"]`; `src/bot/index.ts` exports it from `./path-policy`.

`BASE_PINNED_NAMES`. Target: in `src/bot/path-policy.ts`, `["AGENTS.md", "CLAUDE.md", "GEMINI.md", "codex.md", ".cursorrules", "AGENTS.override.md", "CLAUDE.local.md"]`; exported from `./path-policy`.

Use the existing path-policy unit tests and checkout integration fixture. Paths in contextFiles are repository-rooted; source paths in this description are relative to packages/nax.

[unit] BASE_PINNED_NAMES imported from @/bot equals ["AGENTS.md", "CLAUDE.md", "GEMINI.md", "codex.md", ".cursorrules", "AGENTS.override.md", "CLAUDE.local.md"].

[unit] isPinnedPath("opencode.json") returns true.

userStories.title: Protect agent config and disclose out-of-item fix files
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Refuse agent-configuration/husky changes and disclose pushed changes beyond agreed file locations.

**Motivation** — `fixProtectedPaths` (`src/bot/path-policy.ts`) refuses `.nax/`, `.github/`, `.gitlab/`, `.gitlab-ci.yml` and secret file names only.

**Approach** — **Fix file policy (S6, user ruling 2026-10-24: protected list plus report).** `fixProtectedPaths` also refuses `isPinnedPath` files and anything under `.husky/`; `sensitivePaths` flags the same files in the review summary. Files outside the agreed items are not refused: on a `pushed` outcome the fix summary adds one line listing the changed files no agreed item names, computed in `reportStep` from `state.changed` and the agreed items' `file` fields, so `checkStep` and the graph declarations are unchanged.

**Scope** — In: path-policy filter expansion and reportStep detail rendering using US-001's isPinnedPath; existing policy/check/report tests. Out: US-001 list ownership; US-003/004 pin mechanics; US-005 session wiring; US-006 trust gate. A fix that changes files no agreed item names is reported in the fix summary, never refused (user ruling 2026-10-24); a stricter file scope is not built. Agreed item `file` values and changed paths are compared as spelled for the out-of-item line; a non-canonical spelling such as `./src/a.ts` is not normalised. Git hook managers other than husky (`.githooks/`, `lefthook.yml`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`) are not added to the protected list. `.husky/` is matched at the repo root only, and pinned names match case-sensitively, so a `claude.md` that a case-insensitive filesystem treats as `CLAUDE.md` is neither pinned nor protected.

**Interface** — `fixProtectedPaths(files)` (`src/bot/path-policy.ts`): also keeps a file when `isPinnedPath(file)` or it starts with `.husky/`. Input order and spelling preserved.

`sensitivePaths(files)` (`src/bot/path-policy.ts`): also keeps a file when `isPinnedPath(file)` or it starts with `.husky/`.

`reportStep` (`src/bot/fix-report.ts`). Target: on outcome `pushed`, when at least one agreed item has a `file`, the `changed` files not equal to any agreed item's `file` are rendered as one line `Also changed, not named by an agreed item: ` followed by code-spanned paths (each through `safeCode`, at most 20 shown, the file-local constant `OUT_OF_ITEM_FILES_SHOWN`, then ` and <n> more`), passed to `renderFixSummary` with the other detail lines. Paths are compared as spelled (both are repo-relative); an absent `state.changed` yields no line.

Existing typed signatures remain `fixProtectedPaths(files: readonly string[]): string[]` and `sensitivePaths(files: readonly string[]): string[]`. Narrow AgreedItem to variants with a file field; preserve all existing manifest/secret/control-file behavior and changed-file order.

[unit] fixProtectedPaths([".mcp.json"]) returns [".mcp.json"].

[unit] fixProtectedPaths(["AGENTS.override.md", "opencode.json"]) returns both, in that order.
[unit] fixProtectedPaths(["src/claude.ts", "app/.huskyrc"]) returns [].

[integration] reportStep for outcome pushed, agreed items naming files src/a.ts, and changed ["src/a.ts", "src/b.ts"] posts a fix summary containing the line Also changed, not named by an agreed item: `src/b.ts`.
[integration] reportStep for outcome pushed whose changed files are all named by agreed items posts a summary without a line starting Also changed, not named by an agreed item.
[integration] reportStep for outcome pushed where no agreed item has a file posts a summary without a line starting Also changed, not named by an agreed item.
[integration] reportStep for outcome gates-failed with changed files no agreed item names posts a summary without a line starting Also changed, not named by an agreed item.
[integration] reportStep for outcome pushed with 23 unnamed changed files lists the first 20 and ends that line with ` and 3 more`.
[integration] reportStep renders each unnamed path as backticks around safeCode(path): a changed path src/@alice.ts appears as `${safeCode("src/@alice.ts")}`.

routing.reasoning: Existing policy and reporting extension without a new graph abstraction; protected-path access control requires isolated security TDD.

userStories.title: Guard pinned path parents and fail closed around sessions
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Complete session pinning with link-safe filesystem traversal and a fail-closed generic session scope.

**Motivation** — Pinning cannot reuse the review's `pinInstructions` as-is: it stages the base copies, so `git add -A` or `git commit -a` by the agent would commit them, and `unsafeTree` would report every fix as `dirty`.

**Approach** — A pinned path whose parent inside the worktree is a symlink or a regular file is skipped with a warning, both when pinning and again immediately before each removal at restore (the agent may have swapped a directory for a link during the session). Pathspec arguments to `checkout`, `reset` and `add -N` carry the `:(literal)` magic prefix, so a file name with glob characters matches only itself; `update-index` takes plain paths. Every git call goes through `botGit`.

`restore()` runs `update-index --no-skip-worktree -- <head files + base-only files>` (plain paths), `reset -q HEAD -- <all>` (`:(literal)` pathspecs), removes every path in `paths` whose parents are still real directories (re-checked with `lstat` right before each removal; a linked or non-directory parent is skipped with the same warning), lists the pinned files of the current `HEAD` with `ls-tree -r` and checks them out from `HEAD`; it throws `BOT_SESSION_RESTORE_FAILED` on a git failure. With no pinned file at either side, `pinBaseForSession` runs only the two `ls-tree` calls.

**Scope** — In: extend US-003's session-pin.ts with in-worktree parent lstat checks at pin and restore, safety warnings and basePinScope lifecycle/error precedence; unit scope and real-repo link fixtures. Out: US-003 core Git mechanics already exist; US-005 connects the scope to runBotFix/runBranchFix and prompts. Base pinning skips any pinned path under a symlinked or regular-file parent; the head's file at such a path stays for the session. A fix process killed mid-session leaves its throwaway worktree pinned (skip-worktree set); no recovery path reuses that worktree's index, and the saved fix keeps only the commit.

**Interface** —
```ts
/** pin -> run -> restore; a restore failure is logged and rethrown (fail closed), discarding the run's result. */
export function basePinScope(worktree: string, baseSha: string): <T>(run: () => Promise<T>) => Promise<T>;
```

Use pinBaseForSession(worktree: string, baseSha: string): Promise<SessionPin> and SessionPin.restore(): Promise<void> from US-003. Keep _sessionPinDeps as the external-call seam. A linked or non-directory parent is skipped with `warn("bot-fix", "Skipped pinning a path under a linked or non-directory parent", { path })`; pin or restore continues. Re-check immediately before every removal and avoid checking HEAD configuration out through an unsafe parent. Follow checkout.ts's ENOENT/ENOTDIR handling patterns for missing paths without treating a regular-file parent as a directory.

Failure handling: A git call in pinBaseForSession fails -> NaxError BOT_SESSION_PIN_FAILED (stage bot-fix); basePinScope rejects without running the session. The session (run) rejects -> basePinScope still calls restore(), then rethrows the session's error. restore() fails -> basePinScope logs `warn("bot-fix", "Could not restore head agent configuration after the fix session", { worktree, error })` and rejects with that BOT_SESSION_RESTORE_FAILED error, discarding the run's result; this takes precedence over a run error too. A pinned path has a symlinked or regular-file parent in the worktree, at pin or at restore -> skip that path, emit the warning above and continue. Successful restore returns run's exact value.

routing.reasoning: Extends US-003's single module with parent-path checks and a generic cleanup wrapper rather than changing architecture; symlink safety and session error precedence still require isolated security TDD.

userStories.title: Run fix and repair sessions on base agent configuration
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Wire the session pin into worktree fix and repair calls while restoring head configuration before leftover commits.

**Motivation** — The review pins these from the base; the fix does not.

**Approach** — **Wiring (S5).** `BranchStepContext` gains `sessionScope`; `runBranchFix` runs only `runFixSession` inside it, so `commitLeftovers` sees the head's configuration. `fixCheckout` sets `sessionScope` to `_botFixDeps.basePinScope(checkout.worktree, checkout.baseSha)` unless the checkout is in place (user ruling 2026-10-24: `--in-place` is your own working tree and is not pinned). The fix and repair prompts say the agent configuration is the base's for this session and must not be edited or committed.

**Scope** — In: optional BranchStepContext scope, runBranchFix boundary, _botFixDeps injection and fixCheckout context, pinnedBase prompt input and constant, fixStep/repairStep callers, @/prompts export and end-to-end seam tests. Out: US-003/004 own pin internals, US-002 owns changed-file refusal/reporting, US-006 owns detected-check trust. `nax bot fix --in-place` does not pin the base agent configuration; it runs in the user's own working tree (user ruling 2026-10-24). An agent that deliberately clears `skip-worktree` and commits a pinned file gets its fix refused as `protected`; the pin does not try to prevent that. An uncommitted agent edit to a pinned file is discarded when the head's copy is restored; the fix proceeds without it. The review's own pin (`pinInstructions`) is unchanged apart from reading the longer lists.

**Interface** — `BranchStepContext` (`src/workflow/branch-step-context.ts`) gains
```ts
readonly sessionScope?: <T>(run: () => Promise<T>) => Promise<T>;
```

`runBranchFix` (`src/workflow/branch-fix.ts`). Baseline: `ensureReport`, `runFixSession`, `commitLeftovers`. Target: `runFixSession` runs as `fc.sessionScope ? fc.sessionScope(() => runFixSession(...)) : runFixSession(...)`; `ensureReport` before and `commitLeftovers` after stay outside the scope.

`_botFixDeps` (`src/bot/fix-run.ts`) gains `basePinScope` (from `./session-pin`).

`fixCheckout` (`src/bot/fix-run.ts`, file-local). Baseline env `ctx: { ...context.ctx, runGit: botGit }`. Target: `ctx: { ...context.ctx, runGit: botGit, ...(checkout.inPlace ? {} : { sessionScope: deps.basePinScope(checkout.worktree, checkout.baseSha) }) }`.

`CheckoutStateInput` (`src/prompts/builders/bot-checkout-state-builder.ts`) gains `pinnedBase?: boolean`; with it `renderCheckoutState` appends, as its last line, `PINNED_BASE_NOTE` (new export of that builder file, re-exported from `@/prompts` beside `renderCheckoutState`): "Agent configuration (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and the other instruction files, .claude/, .mcp.json and each agent's config directory) holds the base branch's versions for this session; nax restores the PR's versions afterwards. Do not edit, stage or commit those files."

`fixStep` (`src/bot/fix-steps.ts`) and `repairStep` (`src/bot/repair-step.ts`) pass `pinnedBase: env.checkout.inPlace !== true` to `renderCheckoutState`.

Do not move setup/gates/report creation/auto-commit into the scope, and keep preparePrCheckout(pinBaseFiles:false) for fix: the session scope does the temporary pin. The same env.ctx must flow to repair. A restore failure must propagate from runBranchFix through runBotFix with BOT_SESSION_RESTORE_FAILED and prevent push; do not absorb it into the session's ordinary fixFailure. Extend existing branch-fix/prompt tests and create fix-pinned-session.test.ts. Use shared makeBotFixEnv/makeBotFixDeps runtime fixtures and injectable scopes for fake checkouts; do not run real Git on fixture /repo paths.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] runBranchFix with a sessionScope stub calls it once, and _workflowDeps.callOp runs after the scope started and before it ended.
[unit] runBranchFix with a sessionScope stub and a dirty tree after the session calls _workflowDeps.autoCommitIfDirty after the scope ended.
[unit] runBranchFix without sessionScope calls _workflowDeps.callOp once, as before (regression pin).

userStories.title: Require invocation trust for fixes using detected checks
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add a fix-only --trust flag that explicitly authorizes detected package-script checks.

**Motivation** — On a repo whose base has no nax config and no `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` checks, `resolveBotChecks` falls back to package scripts (`source: "detected"`) and the fix runs.

**Approach** — **`--trust` for detected checks (H13).** `nax bot fix` gains `--trust` (per invocation, never stored). In `fixCheckout`, checks with `source: "detected"` (also when reused from the saved review) refuse the fix unless `input.trust` is true. The flag covers only this case; untrusted PRs are still refused (S11 stays deferred).

**Scope** — In: BotFixInput/BotFixOptions trust, fix-only Commander flag, conditional CLI passthrough, refusal constant/barrel export, refusal after fixChecks and existing none refusal, regression fixture update and cycle passthrough tests. Out: US-005 session pin wiring and US-007 review settlement. `--trust` lifts only the detected-checks refusal; it does not let `nax bot fix` run on an untrusted PR, and sandboxed gates for untrusted PRs (S11) stay deferred. `nax bot review` does not gain `--trust`; a review on detected checks keeps running as today.

**Interface** — `BotFixInput` (`src/bot/fix-run.ts`) gains `readonly trust?: boolean`. `BotFixOptions` (`src/cli/bot.ts`) gains `readonly trust?: boolean`; `registerBotCommand` adds `.option("--trust", "Run on checks detected from package scripts (no nax config on the base branch)")` to the `fix` command only; `botFixCommand` passes `...(options.trust === true && { trust: true })` to `runBotFixCycle`.

`BOT_FIX_DETECTED_REFUSAL` (new export of `src/bot/fix-run.ts` and `@/bot`): "the base branch has no nax config and no AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md checks; run nax setup, or pass --trust to run the package scripts nax detected".

`fixCheckout` (`src/bot/fix-run.ts`, file-local): after the `source === "none"` refusal, a refusal with reason `BOT_FIX_DETECTED_REFUSAL` when `checks.source === "detected"` and `input.trust !== true`.

`runBotFixCycle` (`src/bot/fix-cycle.ts`) is unchanged: it already spreads `input` into the ready pass.

Modify `packages/nax/test/integration/bot/fix-run.test.ts`: the beforeEach env uses checks with source detected, and every test runs runBotFix(input) expecting the fix to proceed; the shared input object gains trust:true so those tests keep running the fix. The invariant each test pins is unchanged. Add fix-trust.test.ts, exercise saved version 3 checks, and retain existing CLI/cycle regression behavior. No trust persistence or artifact format change is needed.

userStories.title: Keep workflow fixes open after reading non-writer comments
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Prevent a review exposed to outsider comments from settling workflow items as fixed.

**Motivation** — The item threads are filtered to writers' replies, but the same review prompt carries every other thread and top-level comment, so an outsider's "B2 is fixed now" can produce that verdict.

**Approach** — **No outsider-driven item settling (S4, user ruling 2026-10-24: fail closed, no extra call).** When the review has open workflow items (`itemEarlier` non-empty), `reviewEnvironment` asks a new `hasNonWriterAuthor` whether any thread, top-level comment or earlier-thread comment the review read was written by someone other than the bot and without write access (the same cached `writerCheck`; a failed check counts as no write access). `PostReviewInput.itemFixedBlocked` carries the answer, and `effectiveEarlier` then treats a `fixed` verdict on a `w-` item as open, so `postEarlier` posts no echo and resolves nothing (one warning) and `earlierCounts` counts it as open in the review summary. `f-` findings and every other verdict are unchanged. A CI bot or any other commenter without write access blocks item settling on that PR; that is the fail-closed ruling.

**Scope** — In: hasNonWriterAuthor and barrel export, conditional reviewEnvironment computation with cached writerCheck, optional posting flag, effectiveEarlier downgrade/blocked marker, single warning, unchanged count/event consumers and runBotReview/postPrReview seam tests. Out: US-008 static intent/confidential issue handling and US-006 fix trust. A `w-` item is not settled by a second, writer-only model call; a blocked `fixed` verdict stays open until a writer rules or `nax bot fix` pushes a fix (user ruling 2026-10-24). `itemFixedBlocked` does not consider linked issue bodies or the PR description; only thread, top-level and earlier-thread comments count.

**Interface** — `hasNonWriterAuthor(comments: readonly PrComment[], login: string, check: WriterCheck): Promise<boolean>` (new export of `src/bot/writers.ts` and `@/bot`): `true` when any comment whose `author` is not `login` fails `check` (passing `{ login: author, id: authorId }`); `false` for an empty list.

`PostReviewInput` (`src/bot/post.ts`) gains `readonly itemFixedBlocked?: boolean`; absent means `false`.

`reviewEnvironment` (`src/bot/review-run.ts`, file-local). Target: when `recorded.itemEarlier` is non-empty, it sets `post.itemFixedBlocked` to `await hasNonWriterAuthor([...items.threads.flatMap((t) => t.comments), ...items.comments, ...postEarlier.flatMap((t) => t.comments)], items.login, writerCheck)`; otherwise it makes no such call.

`effectiveEarlier` (`src/bot/post-earlier.ts`). Target: for a `w-` key with verdict `fixed` and `input.itemFixedBlocked === true`, the entry's `verdict` becomes `{ ...verdict, status: "open" }` and the entry carries `blocked: true` (`EarlierEntry` gains `readonly blocked?: true`). `earlierCounts` and `withdrawalEvents` read the downgraded verdict unchanged.

`postEarlier` (`src/bot/post-earlier.ts`). Target: for each entry with `blocked: true` it calls `getLogger()?.warn("bot-post", "Kept item open: the review read text from someone without write access", { threadId, key })` once; the existing `status === "open"` skip then posts and resolves nothing.

Use the same WriterCheck from triage (forge/access.ts caches per login and resolves rejected checks false); do not add permission queries for irrelevant repliers when there are no open w- items. Existing summary/artifact consumers use effectiveEarlier, so downgrade once there. Preserve f- fixes, w- withdrawals, bot-login exclusion and authorId forwarding. Add item-fixed-blocked.test.ts entering through runBotReview as well as existing writers/post/rulings test extensions.

[integration] That blocked postPrReview posts a review summary whose earlier-findings line counts the item as still open and 0 fixed.
[integration] postPrReview with itemFixedBlocked absent and the same w- thread and fixed verdict posts the wr-fixed-<key> echo and resolves the thread (regression pin).
[integration] postPrReview with itemFixedBlocked: true and an f- earlier thread with verdict fixed still replies and resolves it.

[integration] runBotReview on that PR with a reply by mallory inside another commenter's thread (not top-level) also posts no wr-fixed- comment.
[integration] runBotReview on that PR with a reply by mallory on one of the bot's own f- finding threads also posts no wr-fixed- comment.
[integration] runBotReview on that PR where every other comment's author has write access posts the wr-fixed- echo for the item.
[integration] runBotReview on that PR where _botReviewDeps.hasWriteAccess rejects for mallory posts no wr-fixed- comment.
[integration] runBotReview on a PR without open w- items never calls _botReviewDeps.hasWriteAccess for a thread replier who opened nothing (regression pin of the S3 call count).

userStories.title: Exclude confidential intent, fence CI logs and strip forge tokens
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Keep confidential/untrusted intent out of review prompts, delimit CI log text and remove missing forge tokens from default shell environments.

**Motivation** — `parseReply` (`src/forge/issues.ts`) returns a GitLab issue even when it is confidential, so a fork MR saying "Closes #n" pulls a confidential issue into a review that posts publicly.

**Approach** — **Untrusted inputs (S10, #2639, S9 in nax).** `parseReply` returns `null` for a GitLab issue with `confidential: true`. `ciCheckIssue` wraps the excerpt in `markdownFence`. `reviewEnvironment` passes intent paths only when the review is not static. The `quality.stripEnvVars` default gains `GITLAB_TOKEN`, `GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN` at both places that define it: the field default in `QualityConfigSchema` (`src/config/schemas-execution.ts`) and the `QualityConfigSchema.default({...})` literal in `NaxConfigSchema` (`src/config/schemas.ts`), which is what `DEFAULT_CONFIG` reads.

**Scope** — In: forge issue null filtering/skip warning, CI excerpt fencing, static-review intent omission, both stripEnvVars defaults and existing affected test updates. Out: US-007 outsider item-settlement guard, US-009 glab filesystem deny, US-006 trust flag and US-005 pinned-session prompts. A user or project config that sets `quality.stripEnvVars` replaces the default list, so the three new tokens are not stripped there. The three new `quality.stripEnvVars` tokens are also stripped from nax's own gate and test runs, not just the native agent's Bash; that is intended. CI check names and failed-step names in the CI repair finding are not fenced; only the log excerpt is. Whether each ACP agent's static review really has no network access is not checked here; it needs a per-agent probe. H15 (design decisions read from the PR head) is not changed; `WORKFLOW_DESIGN_DECISIONS_ITEM` already tells the reviewer an edited ADR is not settled authority.

**Interface** — `parseReply` (`src/forge/issues.ts`, file-local): a GitLab reply with `confidential === true` returns `null`. `readLinkedIssues`'s skip warning for a `null` result becomes `"Skipping linked reference: a pull request or a confidential issue"`.

`ciCheckIssue` (`src/workflow/ci-repair-steps.ts`, file-local): the excerpt line becomes `markdownFence(check.excerpt)`; the heading lines are unchanged.

`reviewEnvironment` (`src/bot/review-run.ts`, file-local): It passes `...intent` into the review input only when `staticMode` is false.

`quality.stripEnvVars` default, at both sites: the `stripEnvVars` field default inside `QualityConfigSchema` (`src/config/schemas-execution.ts`) and the `stripEnvVars` array in the `quality: QualityConfigSchema.default({...})` literal of `NaxConfigSchema` (`src/config/schemas.ts`). Each becomes its existing list followed by `"GITLAB_TOKEN", "GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN", "GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN"`.

Unchanged integration: `markdownFence(text): string` (`@/utils/markdown-fence`): fence one backtick longer than the longest run, minimum 3. `featureIntentPaths(checkout)` (`src/bot/intent.ts`). `extractDispatchConfigFields(config).stripEnvVars` (`src/agents/dispatch-config-fields.ts`), which the native agent's Bash strips.

Modify `packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/feature-steps-ci-repair-decision.test.ts` — the mixed-evidence test (about line 138, labelled AC-13 in the CI-repair-decision block), the draft-with-failed-CI test (about line 153, AC-5), and the step-facts tests at about lines 368, 374 and 380 (AC-15, AC-16, AC-17) expect the CI finding's issue to end with the bare excerpt after the heading line (for example the heading `CI check e2e failed:` then `boom`); the excerpt becomes `markdownFence(<excerpt>)`, so each expected issue becomes the heading lines, a newline, then `markdownFence` of the same excerpt. The heading text, the skipped-steps line and their order are unchanged. Extend existing forge issues, review-run/static intent, schema and dispatch tests. ACP's allowlisted buildAgentEnv remains unchanged.

userStories.title: Deny the native sandbox access to glab credentials
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add glab's home-relative credential directory to built-in native sandbox read denies.

**Motivation** — ACP agents get an allowlisted environment with no forge tokens (`buildAgentEnv`, `packages/nax-agent-acp/src/client/env.ts`).

**Approach** — **glab credentials (S9 in nax-agent).** `BUILTIN_CREDENTIAL_READ_DENIES` gains `.config/glab-cli`.

**Scope** — In: packages/nax-agent's sandbox/defaults.ts built-in list and policy-builder assertions using the home fixture, including the existing malformed-home rejection as a negative-path regression. Out: US-008 owns environment-token defaults in packages/nax; no ACP transport changes or new sandbox mechanism. The macOS keychain is not denied to the native agent's shell; `gh` or `glab` reading a keychain token is not blocked by this spec. User documentation of `--trust`, the protected list and the pinned fix session, and the denied read paths list in `docs/guides/sandbox-and-command-safety.md`, are a manual follow-up after merge.

**Interface** — `BUILTIN_CREDENTIAL_READ_DENIES` (`packages/nax-agent/src/sandbox/defaults.ts`): the existing list followed by `".config/glab-cli"`.

`buildSandboxPolicy(input)` (`packages/nax-agent/src/sandbox/policy-builder.ts`): `denyRead` starts with `BUILTIN_CREDENTIAL_READ_DENIES` joined to the home directory.

Keep its existing readonly string-array contract and all existing credential denies; policy-builder already expands and canonicalizes these paths and needs no algorithm change. Use `packages/nax-agent/test/unit/sandbox/policy-builder.test.ts`'s input/home fixture; prove the glab absolute deny and preserve gh. No public exports, API additions or dependency changes are required. Use nax-agent's Node-compatible source conventions and #src/ imports, not nax's @/ aliases. Regression tests must be demonstrated to fail against old code.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] buildSandboxPolicy returns a denyRead containing the input's home directory joined with .config/glab-cli.
[unit] That policy's denyRead still contains the input's home directory joined with .config/gh (regression pin).

[unit] When input.home is an absolute nonexistent path containing a literal asterisk, buildSandboxPolicy throws NaxError with code SANDBOX_POLICY_NOT_LITERAL instead of returning a policy, preserving the existing rejection of non-literal sandbox paths.

routing.reasoning: One additive constant-list change reuses existing policy expansion; credential-store access control still requires the strict security test strategy.

analysis:
This is a security enhancement to existing bot orchestration, not a greenfield subsystem. Navigation used direct reads and searches because codebase-memory MCP is unavailable in this environment. Preserve the binding nine-story decomposition and package workdirs. All nine stories touch an agent security boundary and use three-session-tdd, including the small credential-list change. No implementation code is part of this planning change.

Architecture and conventions: docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:16 identifies the dependency-injection, NaxError, constants and test conventions; docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:95 locates prompt construction in src/prompts. Follow exported _deps seams rather than patching globals, structured logger stages and real-repository integration tests for Git behavior. nax uses Bun and @/ aliases; nax-agent ships Node-compatible source, uses #src/ aliases and explicit .ts extensions on relative source imports. Keep package boundaries intact: this feature needs no nax-ai or ACP changes and no dependency or version changes. nax-agent's list change does not require a new public API. Existing generated instruction files must not be edited. Run targeted bun tests with explicit paths from each story's workdir; never bare bun test. The pipeline handles lint/typecheck/tests. Do not run coverage inside NAX_SANDBOXED=1; outside a nax session, follow each package's coverage rules. nax-agent requires demonstrating that regression tests fail on old code.

US-001/002: packages/nax/src/bot/path-policy.ts:1 is a pure canonical repo-relative path policy. Its current sensitivePaths at :14 only flags control directories and selected manifest names; fixProtectedPaths at :19 additionally blocks secrets but not most instruction/config files. packages/nax/src/bot/checkout.ts:14 and :21 own the two short pinned lists today; :92 matches instruction basenames and :112 implements pinInstructions. Move list ownership to path-policy and add exact case-sensitive root-entry-or-basename matching without normalizing paths. packages/nax/src/bot/index.ts:2 currently re-exports the lists from checkout; :58 exports the policies. Search found no other current list consumers beyond checkout and this barrel. Keep @/bot exports stable while changing their source. The review's existing pin removes symlinks, writes base configuration and stages it (:112-126); do not reuse it as a session pin or alter its algorithm. preparePrCheckout invokes it only when pinBaseFiles is true at checkout.ts:233. Existing real-repo coverage is packages/nax/test/integration/bot/checkout.test.ts:1; its temp repository, local origin and PR refs avoid forge network access. packages/nax/test/unit/bot/path-policy.test.ts:1 already pins order, duplicates, similar-but-unprotected names and permitted manifest edits. Extend these tests rather than replacing existing protection.

packages/nax/src/bot/fix-steps.ts:187 checks clean state and committed changed paths before fixProtectedPaths; :192 uses startHead or reviewed head, with --no-renames delegated to checkout.ts:81, so a move out of a protected location remains visible. Keep checkStep and graph declarations unchanged: expanded policy is sufficient. packages/nax/src/bot/fix-report.ts:302 accepts extra summary detail lines in renderFixSummary and :326 builds them in reportStep. safeCode is already imported at :25. Compute the out-of-item line here only for pushed results, from state.changed and agreed file fields. packages/nax/src/bot/post.ts:20-38 defines the AgreedItem union: finding/thread items can have file while comment items cannot; narrow the union when collecting named files. Existing report/check coverage includes test/integration/bot/fix-report.test.ts, fix-check-steps.test.ts and test/unit/bot/fix-summary.test.ts. Do not introduce a strict agreed-file allowlist.

US-003/004: create src/bot/session-pin.ts, not a modification of the review pin. packages/nax/src/bot/git.ts:3-14 supplies botGit, forwarding to hardened gitWithTimeout with core.hooksPath=/dev/null. Every new Git operation must use _sessionPinDeps.runGit initially identical to botGit. Git tree outputs must be NUL-delimited to preserve arbitrary names. Enumerate HEAD and base with ls-tree -r --name-only -z, retain isPinnedPath results, and operate on their safe union. Base-only files need intent-to-add plus skip-worktree; simply resetting after base checkout leaves untracked base configuration eligible for git add -A. Pathspec-based checkout/reset/add -N require :(literal), while update-index rejects that magic and takes plain paths. A per-worktree info/exclude is not a substitute. Verify actual status, cached diff, agent add/commit and committed blob contents in real repos; argument mocks alone cannot prove index safety. Restore must use the then-current HEAD, not the original head snapshot, so a committed configuration edit survives to the protected-path guard. Clear skip-worktree and drop intent-to-add entries before removing pinned paths and checking HEAD copies out. With no pinned files on either side, pin must issue only the two ls-tree calls.

New integration/bot/fix-pinned-session.test.ts must enter through runBotFix for wiring, in-place bypass, repair reuse and restore-failure no-push proof; also integrate real runBranchFix/basePinScope. Risks and compatibility: Git index manipulation, base-only intent-to-add files, literal pathspecs, changed HEAD during session and link swaps are the highest-risk area; mock failures plus real-Git tests are mandatory. Intentional behavior changes are detected-check fixes requiring --trust, more protected files refusing pushes, outsider-tainted fixed workflow verdicts remaining open, static intent exclusion and default forge-secret stripping. Old optional fields remain backward compatible; absent sessionScope/itemFixedBlocked/pinnedBase retain old behavior. No artifact version migration or trust persistence is introduced. Saved detected checks are deliberately gated too. Explicit stripEnvVars configuration still replaces defaults, and additional stripping also affects nax gates/tests. Restore failure must prevent graph progression and push, not be reduced to dirty/fixFailure. Files outside agreed locations are disclosure-only, not refused. No user documentation, release, issue filing, strict file scope, untrusted-fix execution or other deferred bug fixes are part of implementation. Dependency order is exactly US-001 -> US-002 and US-003 -> US-004 -> US-005; US-006/007/008/009 are independent. Done means all retained spec behaviors and failure-mode behaviors below are satisfied with package-local changes and no expansion of the stated boundary.

Refine-pass self-audit: individually enumerated and retained every original criterion in its binding story: US-001 15, US-002 14, US-003 18, US-004 15, US-005 14, US-006 10, US-007 16, US-008 14, US-009 2 (118 total). Regression qualifiers including root-path-not-name, exact case, input order, as before, still, as today and all regression-pin parentheticals remain attached. All assertions are observable via return/error, call recording, logs, file contents or Git state. US-001/002 have negative match/report cases; US-003/004/005 have injected pin/restore/session errors; US-006 has refusal paths; US-007 has rejected authorization; US-008 has confidential/static-input exclusion. US-009 additionally pins the existing malformed-home rejection: an absolute nonexistent home containing an asterisk must cause SANDBOX_POLICY_NOT_LITERAL, not a weakened policy (policy-builder.ts:78-87). This is a negative-path regression, not a new sandbox algorithm. Failure-table coverage maps pin failure to US-003 and US-004; run-error cleanup to US-004; restore failure/no push to US-004/005; unsafe parents to US-004; committed pinned-file preservation/protection to US-003/002; detected refusal to US-006; failed writer lookup to US-007; confidential null/warning to US-008. All 22 feature exclusions remain verbatim, and no story-local deferral was hoisted. Binding dependencies/workdirs are unchanged. US-005's five context slots now include repair-step alongside branch-fix, fix-run, session-pin and the prompt builder; its simple BranchStepContext declaration remains explicitly specified in the description. US-004 is complex, not expert, because it extends one module; US-008 is medium because its five edits are local guards/helper reuse/default additions. Mandatory security three-session-tdd remains on all nine stories. No source implementation or validation-suite story was added.
outOfScope: `nax bot fix --in-place` does not pin the base agent configuration; it runs in the user's own working tree (user ruling 2026-10-24).
A fix that changes files no agreed item names is reported in the fix summary, never refused (user ruling 2026-10-24); a stricter file scope is not built.
`--trust` lifts only the detected-checks refusal; it does not let `nax bot fix` run on an untrusted PR, and sandboxed gates for untrusted PRs (S11) stay deferred.
`nax bot review` does not gain `--trust`; a review on detected checks keeps running as today.
A `w-` item is not settled by a second, writer-only model call; a blocked `fixed` verdict stays open until a writer rules or `nax bot fix` pushes a fix (user ruling 2026-10-24).
`itemFixedBlocked` does not consider linked issue bodies or the PR description; only thread, top-level and earlier-thread comments count.
Base pinning skips any pinned path under a symlinked or regular-file parent; the head's file at such a path stays for the session.
An agent that deliberately clears `skip-worktree` and commits a pinned file gets its fix refused as `protected`; the pin does not try to prevent that.
Agreed item `file` values and changed paths are compared as spelled for the out-of-item line; a non-canonical spelling such as `./src/a.ts` is not normalised.
A user or project config that sets `quality.stripEnvVars` replaces the default list, so the three new tokens are not stripped there.
Git hook managers other than husky (`.githooks/`, `lefthook.yml`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`) are not added to the protected list.
An uncommitted agent edit to a pinned file is discarded when the head's copy is restored; the fix proceeds without it.
`.husky/` is matched at the repo root only, and pinned names match case-sensitively, so a `claude.md` that a case-insensitive filesystem treats as `CLAUDE.md` is neither pinned nor protected.
A fix process killed mid-session leaves its throwaway worktree pinned (skip-worktree set); no recovery path reuses that worktree's index, and the saved fix keeps only the commit.
The three new `quality.stripEnvVars` tokens are also stripped from nax's own gate and test runs, not just the native agent's Bash; that is intended.
The review's own pin (`pinInstructions`) is unchanged apart from reading the longer lists.
Whether each ACP agent's static review really has no network access is not checked here; it needs a per-agent probe.
The macOS keychain is not denied to the native agent's shell; `gh` or `glab` reading a keychain token is not blocked by this spec.
CI check names and failed-step names in the CI repair finding are not fenced; only the log excerpt is.
A second `nax bot fix` posting duplicate replies on agreed threads, and the other GitLab and rerun-state bugs (C1-C8 of the 2026-10-22 report), are a separate spec.
H15 (design decisions read from the PR head) is not changed; `WORKFLOW_DESIGN_DECISIONS_ITEM` already tells the reviewer an edited ADR is not settled authority.
User documentation of `--trust`, the protected list and the pinned fix session, and the denied read paths list in `docs/guides/sandbox-and-command-safety.md`, are a manual follow-up after merge.
